title: TATAR unified triage summary
description: Shared summary.json contract emitted by every TATAR collector (Windows Tatar.ps1, Linux tatar-linux.sh, and future macOS/Android editions). One parser / dashboard ingests all platforms.

tool.description: Human tool name, e.g. 'TATAR Triage Toolkit'.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS shared schema. Consumers key off this. 1.3 only ADDS optional finding properties, so a 1.2 consumer keeps working against a 1.3 document.

privileged.description: Ran with elevated rights (Administrator on Windows, root on Unix).

durationSeconds.description: Wall-clock collection duration in seconds (unified across platforms).

environment.description: Execution context of the collected host. All fields best-effort; 'unknown'/'none' when undetermined.

virtualization.description: e.g. kvm, vmware, hyperv, xen, none, unknown.

securityModule.description: Linux: selinux-enforcing/permissive, apparmor, none. Windows: defender or none.

modulesSkipped.description: Modules that were requested but never ran (unknown module name). Empty on a clean run. A non-empty list means evidence is MISSING, not absent.

moduleStatus.description: One entry per requested module saying how it ended. status: ok; warn (it finished but logged errors); failed (it crashed, or on Linux its primary artifact was not produced); skipped (requested but never ran - unknown name). Added in 1.6. modulesRun says what was asked for, moduleLimitations says what a module could not do, this says whether it got to finish: an empty section from a 'failed' module is missing evidence, not a clean host. seconds is wall-clock time (one decimal on Windows, whole seconds on Linux).

errors.description: Errors logged while this module ran.

stats.description: Key/value counters. A counter is emitted as a JSON number on every platform. Use the canonical key in x-canonicalStatKeys for a concept any collector can measure, so one dashboard can plot 'accounts on host' without a per-platform special case; a key listed there means the same thing everywhere. Platform-specific counters are allowed, but a new spelling of an existing concept is not.

findingsCount.description: Length of findings[]; equals activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount.

activeFindingsCount.description: Findings still on the headline list. INVARIANT: activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount == findings.length. A low value means 'allowlisted' only when suppressedCount is high - it never means the host is clean.

suppressedCount.description: Findings hidden by an allowlist rule but retained in findings[] for audit. INVARIANT: activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount == findings.length.

moduleLimitations.description: What each module could NOT do on this run: a capped query, a failed fallback, a counter that was never measured, an artifact readable only with privilege the run did not have. Added in 1.4, at module level on purpose - schema 1.3 considered the same information per finding and refused, because "could not read /proc/N" describes a module and would have been copy-pasted onto every finding it touched. Absence of a finding means nothing until you have read this array: a module that collected less than its section header claims is the difference between "clean" and "not looked at".

module.description: The module that was limited. Empty when the limitation applies to the whole run rather than one module (for example: not running with privilege).

limitation.description: What it could not do, in plain words.

findings.description: Automated triage leads (NOT verdicts). Each maps to zero or more MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

severity.description: The shipped collectors emit only High and Review. Info is reserved for low-signal context findings; a consumer may receive it from a future collector, so handle it, but do not expect it today.

category.description: Emitting module/collector, e.g. process, users, persistence.

technique.description: Suggested MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs. Empty when unmapped.

detail.description: Where to look / why it matters.

confidence.description: How sure the tool is (independent of severity). The ladder is fixed and auditable: 0.4 a Review-severity pattern that also occurs benignly, 0.7 a High-severity lead the tool could not confirm, 0.85 two findings from DIFFERENT modules named the same path and a declared correlation rule fired (tool 1.5.0), 0.95 an indicator from the supplied IOC feed matched. The correlation and IOC passes change this number and never the severity.

suppressed.description: True when hidden from the headline by an allowlist rule (still retained for audit).

suppressReason.description: Why the finding was suppressed (allowlist rule / signature).

iocMatch.description: True when an IOC matched this finding. Since 1.3 the indicator itself is in iocIndicator; it is still prefixed into detail as 'IOC match: <indicator> | ...' for human readers.

confidenceReason.description: Why the tool assigned this confidence, in plain words. Derived from the same rule that derives confidence, so the number is auditable without having to read the collector. Added in 1.3; empty when unknown. At 0.85 it names the correlation rule that fired, the two modules that agreed, the shared path and the other finding's id, so the raise can be audited without re-running the collector.

iocIndicator.description: The indicator from the supplied IOC feed that matched, when iocMatch is true; empty otherwise. Before 1.3 this could only be read by parsing the 'IOC match: <indicator> | ...' prefix of detail, which is still written for human readers.

module.description: The collector module that raised this finding, e.g. process, persistence. Added in 1.3; the IOC evidence pass uses 'ioc'.

artifactClass.description: What the evidence IS, as opposed to which module found it. `category` is module-grained - persistence covers Run keys, IFEO, Winlogon, scheduled tasks and COM hijacks at once - so a suppression or IOC rule written against the category cannot aim at one of them. The vocabulary is closed and a collector rejects a value outside it. The shell edition declares a subset of the Windows one - there are no Run keys on Linux - and check_docs_parity.py fails the build if it declares a class Windows does not. 'unknown' is emitted rather than a guess. Added in 1.5.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity of the finding across runs (1.7): SHA-256 of module, artifactClass, category, the message with a PID and counts masked, and the sorted paths. Two scans of the same host give the same fingerprint for the same finding; a different finding never shares one by design of the masking.

contentHash.description: Hash of what the finding says (1.7): severity, confidence and detail. Same fingerprint with a different contentHash means the finding is still there but changed.

evidence.description: Where in this run's evidence the finding came from (1.7): the report file and the section the raising module writes to.

collected_at.description: UTC time the finding was raised, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Earlier than 'generated' by however long the remaining modules took. Added in 1.3.

paths.description: Absolute paths this finding names, de-duplicated, in order of appearance. This is exactly the set the allowlist, publisher, hash and IOC passes can reach, so it is also the audit trail for a suppression decision: a finding with an empty paths[] can never be suppressed by a path, publisher or hash rule. Added in 1.3.

then.description: The three counts are optional for schemaVersion 1.1, which predates them, and mandatory from 1.2 on - every 1.2 producer emits them and four test harnesses assert the invariant.

From schemaVersion 1.4 onward every timestamp in this document is ISO 8601 UTC at second precision - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ - on every platform. Earlier versions are not held to it: the Windows producer wrote local time with an offset while the Linux producer wrote Z, so output from the two editions could not be sorted together and a 1.3 document carried both shapes at once (collected_at in Z beside generated with an offset). Constrained here rather than only described, because 'ISO-8601 string' was what the 1.1 schema already said.
